Subject: MAP: alignment on success signals and close runway

Jonas — thanks for the demo yesterday. We left with enthusiasm but multiple internal stakeholders asked for a concrete checklist they can review with procurement and clinical ops.

Can you and your team provide a short MAP that ties success metrics to acceptance tests and a go/no-go timeline? Specifically, they want:
- 3 primary success metrics we can surface in our executive review
- Concrete acceptance tests we can run during the 4-week pilot (including sample prompts/requests)
- Exit gates that trigger either an extension request or a freeze/rollback
- Approximate close timeline and required procurement steps

We're aiming to present to the execs by Jul 25; ideally we have something to run by Monday so ops can schedule test runs.

Thanks — Sophie
Sophie Clarke
Head of Clinical Programs
Concord Health

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-07-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: alignment on success signals and close runway

Sophie — appreciate the clear asks. I put together a compact "Acceptance Oracle" that maps metrics to runnable tests and a proposed close runway. I attached three artifacts: a one-page MAP timeline, the acceptance oracle workbook (runnable test cases + scoring), and a short SLA exceptions draft you can share with procurement.

Quick highlights:
- Primary success metrics (proposed):
  1) Clinical precision: >= 92% concordance with clinician annotations on a 200-sample set (acceptance threshold 90%).
  2) Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 350ms on representative requests (pilot infra config documented).
  3) Integration stability: zero critical failures in 7-day smoke harness (retries and error rate < 0.2%).

- Acceptance tests (examples included in the oracle):
  • Sample prompt set A (200 records) for concordance scoring (scoring rubric included).
  • Throughput ramp test (10k tokens/hour sustained for a 2-hour window).
  • End-to-end task: clinician-facing summary generation with blind scoring by 3 raters.

- Exit gates:
  • Fail-concordance (final score < 88%): triggers remediation sprint and may extend pilot by 2 weeks.
  • Repeated infra outages (>= 2 incidents > 10min): triggers pause + root cause and potential rollback to read-only mode.
  • Unacceptable latency on >10% of requests during peak windows: triggers configuration change + re-run test.

- Close runway (proposed):
  Week 0 (kickoff) — deploy pilot config and baseline capture
  Week 1 — run sample prompt set A; run smoke harness
  Week 2 — integration tests and clinician blind scoring
  Week 3 — final conformance runs and remediation window
  Week 4 — executive scorecard and procurement handoff

Can you review the attached acceptance oracle (Concord-MAP-acceptance-oracle-v1.xlsx) and tell us whether the clinical precision threshold and the timeline are acceptable? We flex on the exact numbers but want alignment on where to set the go/no-go thresholds so procurement can include the right terms.

I'll be on a short call this afternoon but happy to do 30m tomorrow to walk through.

— Jonas Weber
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Looping in a couple of pragmatic edits from ops:
- Proposal: add a lightweight automated regression check (daily sample of 50 records) so we can detect drift early — passes/fails feed the "integration stability" metric.
- Clarify the acceptance rubric for clinician blind scoring (we recommend Accept / Minor Edit / Major Edit categories; scoring rules inside workbook).
- Suggest an explicit signoff owner from Concord for each gate (clinical lead + procurement rep) — we'll add a signoff column to the workbook.

Also noted that procurement asked about data retention during the pilot — added a note in SLA-exceptions-draft.docx.

Happy to present the workbook in the Friday ops readout if that helps with exec prep.

— Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Ops, Redwood Inference

Thanks Jonas and Lauren — this is exactly what the execs wanted to see. A few quick notes from clinical ops after an internal read:
- The 200-sample concordance set is fine but please ensure 35% of the set contains borderline cases (the ones that tend to diverge between clinicians).
- Can you include an "oracle pass/fail" column that shows the remediation action tied to each failure mode? That will help the review board decide on extension vs no-go quickly.
- Procurement okayed the baseline SLA items; they asked for the pilot to explicitly flag any KMS/HSM dependencies in the SLA exceptions so they can route to security.

Would appreciate an updated workbook by Wed Jul 23 COB so we can finalize the exec packet.

— Sophie
